news.title:
IRB Infrastructure Developers declared a ₹5 dividend with an ex-date of May 26.
Mixed recent returns, but significant growth over the last 5 years noted.

IRB Infra foresees no capital raising; growth via asset rotation.
Assets will move from Private InvIT to Public InvIT, redeploying capital.
Full year 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues miss analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹0.70 (down from ₹5.37 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹78.5b (up 11% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹8.50b (down 87% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 11% (down from 92% in FY 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by higher expenses. Revenue missed analyst estimates by 2.2%. Earnings per share (EPS) also missed analyst estimates by 2.0%. Revenue is forecast to grow 5.1% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 12% growth forecast for the Construction industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 56% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 17% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.
